prerequisites.title: Help Scout account
prerequisites.detail: You need a Help Scout login to open Your Profile > My apps and create the OAuth2 application.

prerequisites.title: Redirect URI from Composio
prerequisites.detail: A redirection URL is required for the Authorization Code flow, so copy it from the Composio dashboard first.

steps.title: Copy redirect URI from Composio
steps.detail: Open the Composio dashboard and copy the callback/redirect URI for a Help Scout auth config.

steps.title: Create the OAuth app in Help Scout
steps.detail: Go to Your Profile > My apps, click Create My App, and paste the redirection URL. Save the generated application ID and secret.
steps.done_when: You hold the application ID and application secret.

steps.title: Create Composio auth config
steps.detail: Create the help_scout auth config through Composio's API with your own client ID and secret.
steps.done_when: The auth config exists in Composio.

steps.title: Test a connection with a real user
steps.detail: Connect a Help Scout user who is an active, invited member of the account and approve on the Authorization screen.
steps.done_when: A connected account is created without a 401 error.

steps.title: Check brand guidelines before launch
steps.detail: If you market the project publicly, read Help Scout's brand guidelines and tell Help Scout when it is finished.

traps.title: Users must be active, invited members
traps.detail: Credentials must belong to an active, invited user in the Help Scout account, otherwise a 401 error is returned. Customers outside such an account may not be able to connect.

traps.title: Do not use a managed app
traps.detail: Composio has no managed Help Scout app, so the connection will not work without your own client ID and secret.

blockers.what_it_means: The credentials are not tied to an active, invited user in the Help Scout account.
blockers.what_to_do: Invite the user to the Help Scout account and make sure they are active, then retry.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: Note that you must have a published branding status before you can request verification for data access.
evidence.answer: A published branding status is required before requesting data access verification in the OAuth Verification Center.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: For example, a project can contain one or more OAuth clients, configure APIs for use by those clients, and configure an OAuth consent screen that's shown to users before they authorize access to your app.
evidence.answer: A Cloud Console project can contain OAuth clients, configure APIs for those clients, and configure the OAuth consent screen.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: If any of your OAuth clients aren't ready for production, we suggest that you delete them from the project that's requesting verification.
evidence.answer: OAuth clients not ready for production should be deleted from the project requesting verification, via the Clients page.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: Branding modifications are not permitted while verification is in progress.
evidence.answer: Branding changes cannot be made while verification is in progress; the ongoing verification must be cancelled first.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: You must limit your use of Google user data to the practices that your published privacy policy discloses.
evidence.answer: The developer must limit use of Google user data to the practices disclosed in the published privacy policy.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: We recommend that you only submit your app for verification if you want to make your app available to any user with a Google Account.
evidence.answer: Developers should submit for verification only if they want the app available to any user with a Google Account.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: You must request the narrowest scope necessary for your app's functionality and ensure data usage complies with API policies and your privacy policy.
evidence.answer: Data usage must comply with API policies and the developer's privacy policy.

items.reason: Quote states the Authorization Code flow is typically used for integrations used by other Help Scout users, matching the statement.
Quote only asks developers to notify Help Scout when a public project is finished; it does not state that no review, verification or partner-acceptance step exists.
Quote says logged-in users will see an Authorization screen, which supports users authorizing the app there.
Quote states credentials must be associated with an active, invited user and a 401 is returned otherwise.
Quote asks developers to read the brand guidelines before launching anything, matching the statement.
Quotes say the flow is used for other users and that the provider should be told when finished, but do not explicitly state that no provider review is needed.
Quotes do not list the ordered steps (create app in My apps, set redirect URL, user authorization); they neither confirm nor contradict the sequence.
Quotes support the self-serve OAuth flow and the notify-after-finish step, but say nothing about 1-2 hours of work; the no-review point is only loosely implied.
